messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: INCIDENT FIRED — canary-deploy-503s (P1). 3 triggers in 2m. Link: https://pd.example/incidents/INC12345
oncall-amber: acked via mobile — investigating, pulling up canary dashboard
kevin: seeing 502/503s on canary nodes in us-west-2. p50 fine, p95 skyrockets. stack: embedger-v2.quant // logs show OOM-ish segfaults?
maria: logs attached from node-3: `2026-03-14T22:45:12Z ERR runtime: SIGSEGV at 0x0` — looks like a native kernel in quant path
sam: @eng-release was this a rolling canary or traffic ramp? any new quant flags turned on?
eng-release: rolling 10% -> 25% this morning, enabled rlhf-quant-speedup flag in config. No kernel changes otherwise.
jen: Support flagged a customer-facing spike: several 5xxs for /v1/embed; Support ticket #SUP-4921 shows 12 users affected, some API retries.
support-bot: Customer-impact summary: 12 unique customers, highest latency 20s, errors 502 x 76 in last 15m. Severity: degradational to user-facing features.
oncall-amber: quick mitigation options: 1) divert canary traffic back to previous model variant; 2) scale canary pool or restart nodes; 3) rollback flag (disable rlhf-quant-speedup). Prefer divert + rollback flag. Thoughts?
kevin: I'm for rollback flag first — it's fast (config flip) and avoids capacity churn. If that fails, divert traffic.
maria: isolate repro: running local with same quant profile reproduces small mems. kernel blame looks plausible. rollback flag will revert to path that avoids quant kernel.
eng-release: patching rollout: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/release/flags -d '{"rlhf-quant-speedup": false}'` — I'll run now and watch.
incident-bot: :information_source: Action: Disable flag requested by eng-release. PD note added.
eng-release: flag disabled, waiting for canary nodes to pick up config (30s).
oncall-amber: monitoring p95 and 5xx count...
kevin: p95 trending down, errors halved after ~45s. node-3 logs: segfaults stop. Looks like flag flip mitigated kernel path.
jen: Support: sending rapid notification to affected customers that we're mitigating and monitoring. No broader impact yet.
product-ops: any risk to dedicated customers or Private tenants?
maria: no, only hosted canary variant with rlhf-quant-speedup enabled. Dedicated/private unaffected.
sam: recommend we hold rollback fully (stop rollout) and revert today's release for the canary cohort. eng-release can coordinate a stop-and-hold.
eng-release: stopping rollout now. Preventing further promotions. Will open a rollback PR to revert the canary change.
kevin: creating temporary alert rule to mute autopage for this aggr pattern until postmortem: `alert: Canaries.503Spike -> suppress 10m if recovery observed` — want to avoid flapping.
oncall-amber: PD: ack remains. I'm going to leave incident open until rollback confirmed in logs and support hears back from customers.
support-bot: Notifying affected customers update: "Mitigation applied, errors reduced. We'll follow up with RCA and ETA for full rollback."
jen: Good. Please capture timeline and affected customers for SOC/CS handoff.
eng-release: rollback PR opened: https://git.dev/repo/pull/987 — kicking off revert.
maria: collect core dumps and kernel trace from nodes for follow-up. I'll attach to the ticket.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Suggestion: schedule postmortem within 48h and owner = maria.
product-ops: assign product outreach to jen for enterprise customers.
oncall-amber: closing loop: errors down to baseline, traffic restored to previous variant, rollback PR opened, customers notified. Leaving incident in "monitoring" for 30m then will resolve if stable.
kevin: quick note for post-incident: add a canary safety gate to disallow that quant flag for full rollout until a kernel-compat test passes.
eng-release: noted. I'll add the safety gate change to the rollback PR.
incident-bot: :tada: Incident status: MONITORING -> next check in 30m. PD incident INC12345 updated.
